value.body: Demand planners estimate future sales for each product and location, so that factories, warehouses and buyers know what to make and stock. Consumer goods, pharma, retail and e-commerce companies hire them. The day involves working with sales data, meeting sales and marketing teams, and adjusting forecasts.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA, B.Com, B.Tech or a supply-chain specialisation

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, ERP and planning systems, dashboards

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as planning analysts or supply-chain trainees and move into demand planning after learning the product range. Strong Excel skills and comfort with numbers help in interviews.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Spreadsheet modelling and basic forecasting methods

value.title: At a glance
items: Forecasts are never exact; the job is about reducing error and explaining it.
Next steps: senior planner, supply planner, or S&OP manager.
An MBA in operations is a common later step but not required to start.
